title: When the Protocol Burns Anew
premise: Silas Yarrow, a disgraced intelligence analyst living under a scrubbed identity, receives a meeting request from a handler who died a decade ago. Following it pulls them into the orbit of the Protocol, a buried program that manufactures false identities for state enemies—and Silas's own past is one of its products. Hunted by the agency that erased them and shadowed by a rogue cell of Protocol survivors who've become the family they never had, Silas must decide whether to sell the program's master key to save their new family or burn it to free everyone trapped inside fabricated lives. In the end, Silas chooses to detonate the archive publicly, sacrificing their own true identity—which never existed—to give the others real ones.
about_author: Paloma Okafor is a former records archivist turned novelist who writes thrillers about people whose paperwork outlives their memories. She splits her year between Lagos and Lisbon, where she collects expired passports from flea markets as research material.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. Ten years into a quiet life as a compliance auditor, Silas receives a calendar invite from Handler Marek Voss—dead since 2015—for tomorrow, 6 p.m., a place that no longer exists. The emotional beat is dread sharpening into reluctant curiosity: someone knows what Silas was made to forget.

chapters.title: Rules of Disappearance
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. Flashbacks interleave with Silas's meticulous counter-surveillance routines as they verify the invite's authenticity through old tradecraft. Every check confirms it: the encryption is Voss's own. Beat: the past isn't knocking; it's already inside the walls.

chapters.title: Empty Chair
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. At the demolished site, Silas finds not Voss but a young woman, Wren, wearing Voss's signet ring and claiming to be his protégée. She says Voss left Silas something before he died. Beat: suspicion wars with hunger for answers about who Silas really was.

chapters.title: What Voss Left Behind
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. A dead-drop yields a partial file on 'Subject Y-7'—a child given a constructed identity by the Protocol. Silas reads their own birth certificate and recognizes the forgery in the ink patterns. Beat: vertigo; the self was always a document.

chapters.title: The Watchers Notice
chapters.summary: POV: Deputy Director Hale. Inside the agency, Hale flags anomalous access to sealed Protocol archives and orders surveillance on Silas. We see the machinery of institutional power deciding, casually, that Silas is now an asset to be managed or removed. Beat: cold menace.

chapters.title: Found People
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. Wren brings Silas to the safehouse: four Protocol survivors—a forger named Teodor, ex-courier Mabel, hacker Juno, and Wren—who operate as a makeshift family. For the first time, Silas is among people who understand being invented. Beat: tentative belonging.

chapters.title: The Master Key
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. Voss's legacy is revealed: half of a cryptographic key that can unseal the Protocol's identity archive—every fabricated life, including proof of who assigned them. Silas holds the other half without knowing it, embedded in their original designation. Beat: burden of leverage.

chapters.title: A Buyer in the Dark
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. A broker called Lysander contacts the safehouse offering millions for the key on behalf of unnamed principals. Wren hides the approach from Silas, rationalizing it as protecting the family. Beat: love curdling into secrecy—the first crack in found family.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. Silas spots agency surveillance on Juno and runs a counter-operation to shake it, burning a decade of careful habits in one night. Hale's team loses them but confirms Silas has allies. Beat: exhilaration and terror of being visible again.

chapters.title: Interrogation of Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. Silas tracks down Voss's widow, learning Voss didn't die—he defected, then was killed trying to protect the archive. His last message names Silas as 'the one who can end it.' Beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Hale's Offer
chapters.summary: POV: Hale. Hale confronts Silas privately: hand over the key, get reinstatement, a real identity, a clean slate. It's everything Silas spent ten years wanting, offered by the people who stole the first one. Beat: temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: Fracture Lines
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Silas discovers Wren's secret negotiations with Lysander; the safehouse erupts. Teodor sides with selling, Mabel with burning, Juno with running. Beat: the family fractures along the same fault lines as the institutions that made them.

chapters.title: Paper Trail
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. Digging into Lysander's buyer, Silas uncovers the Protocol never ended—it was privatized, and the buyers intend to use the key to manufacture identities at scale for sale to the highest bidder. Beat: the horror isn't the past; it's the business model.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: POV: Juno. Agency raid on the safehouse. Juno covers the family's escape but is captured, buying minutes with her freedom. Beat: sacrifice as proof of family—Juno chose them over herself.

chapters.title: Negotiating With Wolves
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. Silas meets Lysander alone, stalling while tracing him, and learns Hale's agency is one of Lysander's clients—the hunters and buyers are the same beast. Beat: betrayal confirmed; there is no clean side to join.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Against orders, Wren and Silas pull Juno from a black-site transit using forged credentials—Teodor's finest work. The op succeeds but exposes Teodor's face to Hale's cameras. Beat: unity reforged in fire, at cost.

chapters.title: Two Halves
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. Assembled, the key reveals the archive's location beneath the decommissioned Voss facility—and a kill-switch Voss built: full public release, irreversible. Silas realizes they were designed as the failsafe all along. Beat: destiny reframed as design.

chapters.title: The Price of Names
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. The catch: releasing the archive publishes every Protocol record—including Silas's, erasing any claim to a private self forever. Hale offers one final deal: silence in exchange for the family's safety. Beat: the theme crystallized—identity versus power.

chapters.title: Burning the Protocol
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. Climax. Silas infiltrates the facility during a buyer auction, evades Hale, and triggers Voss's release as Hale closes in. The archive floods every open channel worldwide. Beat: catharsis—truth as detonation.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Investigations ignite globally; Hale resigns rather than face hearings; Lysander vanishes. The survivors scatter to begin real lives with real names. Beat: exhausted relief, mourning the anonymity they can never reclaim.

chapters.title: Paloma Okafor
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. Epilogue. Silas, legally nameless, adopts a pen name and begins writing the story itself—found family as the only identity that survives documentation. Wren visits with coffee and news of the others. Beat: quiet joy; the self rebuilt by choice, not assignment.

chapters.title: When the Protocol Burns Anew
chapters.summary: POV: Silas. Coda. A new invitation arrives—from someone claiming the Protocol survived in fragments abroad. Silas smiles, closes the laptop, and chooses, this once, not to open it. Beat: hard-won peace held lightly, with the door left ajar for the reader's imagination.
